questions.question: In 1996, Dr. Indira PP Bora, an exponent of Sattriya, was honoured with the
questions.questionHtml: In 1996, Dr. Indira PP Bora, an exponent of Sattriya, was honoured with the
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Sangeet Natak Akademi Award.

Key Points

  • Indian Satriya dancer Dr. Indira P. P. Bora is from Assam. 
  • She received 13 years of training in Bharatnatyam from Guru Rukmini Devi Arundale and Kuchipudi from Guru Vempati Chinna Satyam.
  • Bora has performed and promoted Satriya in Vietnam, the United States, and New Zealand.
  • She was awarded various awards including the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award in 1996 and Padma Shri in 2020.

Additional Information

  • Sattriya Dance has its origin in the ‘Sattras’ established by Mahapurush Srimanta Sankardev in the 15th and 16th centuries. 
    • The Sattras were established for the propagation of Vaishnavism and later became the religious, cultural and social hub of Assam.
    • The Sattriya dance can be classified into two styles, namely ‘Paurashik Bhangi’ i.e. Tandava or Masculine style and ‘Stri Bhangi’ i.e. Lashya or feminine style.
    • On November 15 in the year 2000, the Sangeet Natak Akademi of India recognized Sattriya as one of the eight classical dances of India.
  • ​Sangeet Natak Akademi:
    • It is the apex body in the field of performing arts in the country and was set up in 1953 for the preservation and promotion of the vast intangible heritage of India’s diverse culture expressed in forms of music, dance and drama.
    • The Chairman of the Akademi is appointed by the President of India for a term of five years.
    • Sangeet Natak Akademi is an autonomous body of the Ministry of Culture, Government of India.
    • The registered office of the Akademi is at Rabindra Bhavan, New Delhi.
  • The Sangeet Natak Akademi Awards are the highest national recognition conferred on practicing artists.
    • It is India's National Academy of Music, Dance & Drama, also called the Akademi Puraskar.
    • It is the greatest honor bestowed upon those involved in the performing arts in India.
    • 1952 marked its initial award.

questions.question: Which folk music is a mix of Indian and western music and is popular in Goa?
questions.questionHtml: Which folk music is a mix of Indian and western music and is popular in Goa?
questions.solution: Mando is a unique folk music form that blends Indian and western music, particularly popular in Goa. It features instruments like guitars, violins, and traditional Indian instruments. Originating during the Portuguese colonial era in Goa, Mando includes themes of love, historical events, and social issues. This genre is melodically and harmonically rich and is often performed at weddings, festivals, and cultural events, including the Goan Carnival. Efforts are ongoing to preserve and promote this distinctive musical tradition.

questions.question: Which dancing form is classified as Ekaharya?
questions.questionHtml: Which dancing form is classified as Ekaharya?
questions.solution: Bharatanatyam is the Indian classical dance form classified as Ekaharya, where a single dancer plays multiple roles in one performance. It is popular in Tamil Nadu and Karnataka, known for storytelling, footwork, hand movements, facial expressions, and acrobatics. The Brihadeeswara Temple in Thanjavur has been a center for Bharatanatyam since 1000 CE. The Tanjore Quartette shaped its current repertoire in the early 19th century. The Abhinaya Darpana by Nandikesvara is a key text for studying Bharatanatyam's techniques. Other classical dances include Odissi from Odisha, Sattriya from Assam, and Kathak from Uttar Pradesh.

questions.question: Sitara Devi was famous for which of the following classical dances?
questions.questionHtml: Sitara Devi was famous for which of the following classical dances?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Kathak.

Key Points

  • Sitara Devi was known for Kathak, which is a classical dance form of North India that involves storytelling, intricate footwork, and graceful movements of hands and arms.
  • Sitara Devi was a world-famous Kathak dancer, singer, and actress.
    • She was born to her father Sukhdev Maharaj and her mother was Matsya Kumari on 8 November 1920 in Kolkata.
    • She is known as "Queen of Kathak"
    • She was also referred to as the "Empress of Dancing" or "Nritya Samrajni" by Rabindranath Tagore.
    • She was the recipient of several awards and accolades like the Sangeet Natak Academy award (1969), Padma Shri(1973), Kalidas Samman 1995, and Nritya Nipuna.
    • She died at the age of 94 on November 25, 2014.
  • Kathak is a classical dance form of North India basically Uttar Pradesh.
    • It is a storytelling dance that involves intricate footwork, spins, and graceful movements of the hands and arms.
    • The themes of Kathak are often romantic or devotional in nature.

Additional Information

  • Kathakali is a classical dance form of Kerala.
    • It is a highly stylized and ritualistic dance drama that combines elements of ballet, opera, masque, and pantomime.
    • The performers wear elaborate costumes and makeup to depict characters from Indian mythology.
  • Bharatnatyam is a classical dance form of Tamil Nadu.
    • It is a highly expressive dance that involves intricate footwork, hand gestures, and facial expressions.
    • The themes of Bharatnatyam are often devotional in nature, and the dance is often performed in temples.
  • Manipuri is a classical dance form of Manipur.
    • It is a graceful and fluid dance that involves delicate hand gestures, flowing movements, and intricate footwork.
    • The themes of Manipuri are often mythological or devotional in nature.

questions.question: Hojagiri is a famous dance form of which of these states?
questions.questionHtml: Hojagiri is a famous dance form of which of these states?
questions.solution:
The Correct Answer is "Tripura".Key Points 

  • Hojagiri is a folk dance performed in the state of Tripura by the Reang people.
  • Reang is one of the 21 scheduled tribes of the Indian state of Tripura.
  • The dance is performed by women and young girls, about 4 to 6 members in a team, singing, balancing on an earthen pitcher, and managing other props such as a bottle on the head and earthen lamp on the hand, while only the lower half of the body is moved.
  • It is attractive due to its melodious songs accompanied by bamboo flute, cymbals, and the khamb.
  • The dance is performed during the Hojagiri festival or Laxmi Puja held on the following full moon night of Durga Puja, generally after 3rd day of Dashera.
  • The Goddess Mailuma, (Laxmi) is worshipped on this day.
  • The whole of the Huk or Jhum cultivation is exhibited through this dance.

Additional Information

  • Tripura : 
    • ​Capital - Agartala
    • Main folk dances: Hozagiri dance of Reang community, Garia, Jhum, Maimita, Masak Sumani and Lebang boomani dances of Tripuri community, Bijhu dance of Chakma community, Cheraw and Welcome dances of Lusai community Hai-Hak dance of Malsum community, Wangala dance of Garo Community etc.

questions.question: For contribution to which dance was Tanjore Balasaraswati awarded the title of Sangita Kalanidhi by Madras Music Academy in 1973?

questions.question: Which of the following dances is popularly known as the Gotipua Dance?
questions.questionHtml: Which of the following dances is popularly known as the Gotipua Dance?
questions.solution: Bandha Nritya or Gotipua dance is a popular dance form of Odisha, where young boys dress as women to praise Jagannath and Krishna. It involves acrobatic movements inspired by Radha and Krishna's life. Raghurajpur, Odisha, is famous for its Gotipua dance troupes, while Garba, Bhangra, and Lavani are traditional folk dances of Gujarat, Punjab, and Maharashtra respectively.

questions.question: In which of the following dance forms women imitate parrots as part of the performance?
questions.questionHtml: In which of the following dance forms women imitate parrots as part of the performance?
questions.solution: The question focuses on identifying the dance form where women imitate parrots. Suwa, a traditional dance of Chhattisgarh, involves women mimicking parrots during performances. It is performed as part of worship rituals to honor local deities, highlighting the cultural connection between dance and spiritual practices in the region.

questions.question: Meenakshisundaram Pillai, a dance guru from the village of Pandanallur, was famous for which of the following dance forms?
questions.questionHtml: Meenakshisundaram Pillai, a dance guru from the village of Pandanallur, was famous for which of the following dance forms?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Bharatnatyam.Key Points

  • Meenakshisundaram Pillai was widely recognised for Bharatnatyam, which is a classical dance form originating from Tamil Nadu, India.
  • He was a descendant of the Thanjavur Quartet, a group of four brothers who were court composers in the early 19th century. 
  • He trained many famous Bharatanatyam dancers, including Devadasis like Pandanallur Jayalakshmi and Thangachi Ammal. 
  • He also trained other dancers, including Mrinalini Sarabhai, Rukmini Devi, and Tara Chaudhri. 
  • Pillai's son-in-law, Chokkalingam Pillai, became the doyen Guru of the Pandanallur style after him
  • Bharatnatyam is known for its intricate footwork, hand gestures, facial expressions and body movements that narrate a story or convey a message.

Additional Information

  • Mohiniyattam​
    • Mohiniyattam is one of the two classical dance forms that originated in Kerala, the other one being Kathakali.
    • Mohiniyattam gets its name from the word ‘Mohini’, the feminine form of Lord Vishnu, the word means ‘dance of Mohini’.
    • Dr. Sunanda Nair became the first in India to acquire a Master’s degree in Mohiniyattam. She completed her Ph.D. thesis in Intrinsic Lyrical Feminism in Mohiniyattam from Mumbai University.
    • Mohiniyattam is based on Natya Shastra’s lasya style. 
    • It has delicate movements and more feminine facial expressions.
    • The movements are gentle and glide-like. They do not have terse rhythmic steps. 
    • More emphasis is on the facial expressions and hand gestures
  • Odissi 
    • Odissi, a renowned classical dance form of India, hails from the beautiful state of Odisha.
    • Known for its sensuousness and lyrical beauty, this dance form, often depicted as a dance of love, seamlessly blends the human and divine aspects of life.
    • It beautifully captures the subtle nuances of life, as well as the everyday mundane.
    • The origins of Odissi can be traced back to an early dance style known as Odhra Magadha.
    • This style is referred to as the southeastern style of classical dance in the Natya Shastra, which describes various dance forms.

questions.question: The folk dance of Chavittukali is associated with which of the following Indian states?
questions.questionHtml: The folk dance of Chavittukali is associated with which of the following Indian states?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Kerala.

Key Points

  • Chavittukali:-
    • It is a traditional folk dance form that originated in the state of Kerala, India.
    • It is believed to have been introduced by the Portuguese during their colonial rule in the region.
    • The dance is characterized by its use of distinct footwear called "chavittu" that produces a rhythmic sound when struck against the ground.
    • Chavittukali is typically performed during Christian festivals and celebrations in Kerala.

questions.question: Shovana Narayan an officer with the Indian Audit and Account Services, has won many awards for her contribution to the field of dance at the international level and has recently acted in a movie. She is an exponent of which of the following dance forms?
questions.questionHtml: Shovana Narayan an officer with the Indian Audit and Account Services, has won many awards for her contribution to the field of dance at the international level and has recently acted in a movie. She is an exponent of which of the following dance forms?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Kathak .

Key Points

  • Kathak:

    • Shovana Narayan is a renowned exponent of Kathak, a classical Indian dance form originating from North India.
    • She is known for her graceful movements, expressive storytelling, and technical mastery of Kathak.
    • She has performed extensively both in India and internationally, contributing to the global recognition of Kathak.
    • Beyond performing, she has also contributed to Kathak through choreography, teaching, and writing.
    • She has also explored contemporary themes within her Kathak performances.

Additional Information

  • Bharatanatyam:

    • Bharatanatyam is a classical Indian dance form originating from Tamil Nadu, South India.
    • It is characterized by its intricate footwork, expressive hand gestures (mudras), and facial expressions (abhinaya).
    • Bharatanatyam is known for its emphasis on rhythmic precision and storytelling through dance.
    • It is traditionally a solo dance performed by women.
    • The dance form has a strong spiritual and devotional element.

  • Odissi:

    • Odissi is a classical Indian dance form originating from Odisha, East India.
    • It is characterized by its graceful movements, fluid postures, and sculptural poses.
    • Odissi is known for its lyrical quality and its emphasis on expressing emotions through dance.
    • It's known for it's tribhanga posture.
    • The dance has a strong connection to the temples of Odisha.

  • Kuchipudi:

    • Kuchipudi is a classical Indian dance form originating from Andhra Pradesh, South India.
    • It is characterized by its vibrant movements, fast-paced rhythms, and theatrical elements.
    • Kuchipudi often incorporates storytelling and dramatic expression, including dialogues and songs.
    • It can be performed as a solo, or group performance.
    • It is known for it's use of Tarangam, where the dancer performs on the edge of a brass plate.

questions.question: Which of the following is the unique dance tradition of Himachal Pradesh?
questions.questionHtml: Which of the following is the unique dance tradition of Himachal Pradesh?
questions.solution: The unique dance tradition of Himachal Pradesh is Nati. It is the most famous folk dance in the region, performed by a group of people accompanied by musicians. The dancers' attire reflects the gaddi or Himachali culture. Other dances mentioned for context include Bihu from Assam, characterized by energetic movements and traditional instruments, Cheraw from Mizoram, known for its use of bamboo sticks, and Dandari from Telangana and Andhra Pradesh, which involves storytelling through music and movement.

questions.question: Which of the following dances is listed in the UNESCO List of Intangible Cultural Heritage of India since 2010?
questions.questionHtml: Which of the following dances is listed in the UNESCO List of Intangible Cultural Heritage of India since 2010?
questions.solution: Kalbelia dance, listed in the UNESCO List of Intangible Cultural Heritage of India since 2010, is associated with the Kalbelia tribe of Rajasthan. Known for its graceful, snake-like movements, it is often called the "snake charmer dance." Performed by both men and women, women wear traditional black skirts with silver jewelry and embroidery. Instruments like the 'pungi,' 'dholak,' and 'khanjari' accompany the dance. The UNESCO list aims to protect and promote important cultural practices, with India also having Yoga, Kumbh Mela, and Vedic chanting inscribed. This inclusion aids in preserving these traditions for future generations.

questions.question: Terah taali dance belongs to which of the following states?
questions.questionHtml: Terah taali dance belongs to which of the following states?
questions.solution: Terah taali is a traditional folk dance from Rajasthan, notable for its unique performance involving thirteen cymbals tied to different parts of the performers' bodies, which they strike in rhythm while dancing. This dance is primarily performed by the Kamar tribe and is often dedicated to the folk deity Baba Ramdev.

questions.question: With which Indian state is the ‘Panthi’ dance form associated?
questions.questionHtml: With which Indian state is the ‘Panthi’ dance form associated?
questions.solution: Panthi dance is performed by Satnami community in Chhattisgarh conveying spiritual teachings through music and lyrics. Other famous dances in Chhattisgarh include Saila, Karma, Sua Nacha, Raut Nacha, and more. Maharashtra, Punjab, and Kerala have their own famous dances like Lavani, Koli, Bhangra, Giddha, Mohiniyattam, Theyyam, Koodiyattam, Chakyar Koothu, and Ottamthullal.

questions.question: What is the traditional bamboo dance of Mizoram called?
questions.questionHtml: What is the traditional bamboo dance of Mizoram called?

  • Cheraw is a very old traditional dance of Mizoram.

questions.question: Which of the following folk dance is related to state of Maharashtra?
questions.questionHtml: Which of the following folk dance is related to state of Maharashtra?
questions.solution: Lezim is a folk dance from Maharashtra, India, where dancers use an instrument called a Lezim or lezium, a wooden stick with jingling cymbals. The dance is vigorous and involves many calisthenic moves, often performed during the Ganesh festival. Other folk dances from Maharashtra include Lavani, Nakata, Koli, Gafa, and Dahikala. Chhau is a semi-classical Indian dance with martial and folk traditions, with three styles: Purulia Chhau (West Bengal), Seraikella Chhau (Jharkhand), and Mayurbhanj Chhau (Odisha). Munari and Painka are also folk dances in India but not specific to Maharashtra.

questions.question: Who among the following invented and perfected India’s classical dance form Sattras?
questions.questionHtml: Who among the following invented and perfected India’s classical dance form Sattras?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Srimanta Sankardev.

Key Points

  • Srimanta Sankardev invented and perfected India’s classical dance form Sattras.
  • It is believed that Bharatnatyam was revealed by Lord Brahma to Bharata, a famous sage who then codified this sacred dance in a Sanskrit text called the Natya Shastra.
  • Sattriya is a classical Indian dance that originated in its eastern state of Assam.
  • There are nine classical dance forms in India, which include Bharatnatyam, Kathak, Kathakali, Kuchipudi, Manipuri, Mohiniyattam, sattriya, and chhau.
  • Bharatanatyam is the first classical dance practice in India. The dance form was predominant in primeval Tamil Nadu, and numerous records have veiled them such as Natya Shastra.

Additional Information

  • K. Uma Rama Rao born Uma Maheshwari on 4 July 1938 – 27 August 2016 was an Indian Kuchipudi dancer, choreographer, research scholar, author, and dance teacher.
  • She was also the Founder & Director of Lasya Priya Dance Academy, established in 1985 in Hyderabad, India.
  • Uday Shankar was an artist, dancer, and choreographer who popularized Indian dance through his effective use of western theatrical techniques in combination with classical Indian dance.
  • Uday Shankar (8 December 1900 – 26 September 1977) was an Indian dancer and choreographer.
  • Uday Shankar was the first to bring the concept of modern dance to India with his novel approach and works
  • Guru Gopinath was an exponent of various styles of Indian dances. The illustrious 'Raam Leela' of Delhi, choreographed and directed by him was its glorious proof.

questions.question: Jawara dance is a popular folk dance of _________.
questions.questionHtml: Jawara dance is a popular folk dance of _________.
questions.solution: Jawara dance is a popular folk dance of Madhya Pradesh, particularly in the Bundelkhand region. It celebrates a good harvest, symbolizing joy and prosperity among farming communities. Performers carry baskets filled with crops, mainly jawara (barley), on their heads, accompanied by lively music and rhythmic movements. This dance contrasts with the classical and folk dances of other states such as Kathakali and Mohiniyattam in Kerala, Nati in Himachal Pradesh, and Garba in Gujarat. Each of these states has its distinct dance traditions, different from the Jawara dance of Madhya Pradesh.

questions.question: Gugga is the famous ritualistic dance of ________, which is performed in the procession taken out in memory of Gugga Pir.
questions.questionHtml: Gugga is the famous ritualistic dance of ________, which is performed in the procession taken out in memory of Gugga Pir.
questions.solution: Gugga is a famous ritualistic dance performed in Haryana during the procession in memory of Gugga Pir, a revered warrior saint also known as Gugga Jaharpir. The dance is an essential part of the Gugga Naumi festival, held in the monsoon season, and reflects local traditions and community devotion. The festival and dance aim to seek blessings and protection from Gugga Pir against snake bites and other misfortunes.

questions.question: Match the following performances of Indian naatya, which were presented by the means of variegated components: (1) Angika (a) costumes and make-up (2) Vachika (b) depiction of mental or psychological states (3) Aharya (c) spoken words (4) Sattvika (d) gestures and other bodily movements
questions.questionHtml:
Match the following performances of Indian naatya, which were presented by the means of variegated components:

(1)

Angika

(a)

costumes and make-up

(2)

Vachika

(b)

depiction of mental or psychological states

(3)

Aharya

(c)

spoken words

(4)

Sattvika

(d)

gestures and other bodily movements
questions.solution:
The correct answer is 1 - d, 2 - c, 3 - a, 4 - b.

Key Points

  • Angika refers to the expression through gestures and other bodily movements. Hence, 1 matches with d.
  • Vachika pertains to spoken words. Hence, 2 matches with c.
  • Aharya involves costumes and make-up. Hence, 3 matches with a.
  • Sattvika is about the depiction of mental or psychological states. Hence, 4 matches with b.

Additional Information

  • Natyashastra:
    • The Natyashastra is an ancient Indian treatise on the performing arts, encompassing theatre, dance, and music. It was written by the sage Bharata Muni.
    • The treatise is considered the foundation of classical Indian dance and theatre.
  • Components of Natyashastra:
    • Angika: Bodily movements, gestures, and expressions.
    • Vachika: Use of voice and spoken words.
    • Aharya: Costumes, make-up, and accessories.
    • Sattvika: Emotional expressions and depiction of psychological states.

questions.question: Which among the following classical dance forms was introduced in the 16th century by Vaishnava saint Mahapurusha Sankaradeva?
questions.questionHtml: Which among the following classical dance forms was introduced in the 16th century by Vaishnava saint Mahapurusha Sankaradeva?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Sattriya.

Key Points

  • The great Assamese reformer and Vaishnava saint Mahapurusha Sankaradeva established the Sattriya dancing style in the 15th century A.D. as a potent means of spreading the Vaishnava religion.
  • It is one of India's eight classical dance genres.
  • Sankaradeva created this dance style by fusing ideas from numerous treatises with popular dance styles, regional folk dances, and his own unique perspective.
  • The Sattriya dance is a blatant example of how the former influenced the latter.
  • Bihu, Bodos, and other Assamese folk dances are other clearly discernible influences on Sattriya dance.
  • These dancing styles have very similar hand movements and rhythmic syllables.

questions.question: Which form of Indian dance is said to be ‘soft and suitable for female presentation’?

questions.solution:
The correct answer is Laasya

Key Points

  • Laasya is a form of Indian dance that is said to be 'soft and suitable for female presentation'.
  • It is often associated with gentle, graceful movements and expressions.
  • Laasya contrasts with Taandava, which is considered vigorous and more suitable for male dancers.
  • This dance form is deeply rooted in Indian classical dance traditions and is often seen in performances depicting feminine grace and beauty.

Additional Information

  • Indian classical dance encompasses various dance forms, each with its unique style and cultural significance.
  • Some of the prominent classical dance forms include Bharatanatyam, Kathak, Odissi, Kathakali, Manipuri, Kuchipudi, and Mohiniyattam.
  • These dance forms are known for their intricate footwork, expressive gestures, and elaborate costumes.
  • Classical dances in India are often performed during religious ceremonies, festivals, and cultural events.

questions.question: 'Powada dance' is a performing art from the state of ________ .
questions.questionHtml: 'Powada dance' is a performing art from the state of ________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Maharashtra.

  • Powada is the traditional folk art from Maharashtra.

Key Points

  • The word Powada itself means “the narration of a story in glorious terms”.
    • Th e narratives are always odes in praise of an individual hero or an incident or place.
    • The chief narrator is known as the Shahir who plays the duff to keep the rhythm.
    • The tempo is fast and controlled by the main singer who is supported by others in the chorus.
    • The earli est notable Powada was the Afzal Khanacha Vadh (The Killing of Afzal Khan) (1659) by Agnidas which recorded Shivaji’s encounter with Afzal Khan.

Additional Information

  • List of folk dances of different states in India:
    • Gujarat - Garba, Dandiya Ras, Tippani Juriun, Bhavai.
    • Rajasthan - Ghumar, Chakri, Ganagaur, Jhulan Leela, Jhuma, Suisini, Ghapal, Kalbeliya.
    • Kerala - Kathakali (Classical), Ottam Thulal, Mohiniattam, Kaikottikali.
    • Maharashtra - Lavani, Nakata, Koli, Lezim, Gafa, Dahikala Dasavtar or Bohada.

questions.question: What are the two main parts corresponding to Lasya and Tandava elements in Manipuri dance?
questions.questionHtml: What are the two main parts corresponding to Lasya and Tandava elements in Manipuri dance?
questions.solution: Manipuri dance, known as Jagoi, is a classical dance form from Manipur. It consists of two main elements: Jagoi and Cholom. Jagoi represents the gentle and graceful Lasya aspect, typically performed by female dancers, while Cholom signifies the dynamic and vigorous Tandava aspect, usually performed by male dancers. These elements embody the dual nature of the dance, blending softness and strength. Manipuri dance is deeply rooted in regional rituals and traditions, featuring fluid movements, delicate hand gestures, and expressive facial expressions. Its unique costumes and musical instruments contribute to its distinct cultural identity.

questions.question: Which traditional dance of Goa is performed during the Shigmo festival?
questions.questionHtml: Which traditional dance of Goa is performed during the Shigmo festival?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is Morulem.

Key Points

  • Shigmo or Shishirotsava is a spring festival celebrated in the Indian state of Goa
  • It is one of the major festivals of the Hindu community.
  •  It is also celebrated by the Konkani diaspora and the Indian festival of Holi is part of it.
  • Shigmo festivals also continue in various rural parts of Goa, spanning over a fortnight, with different days earmarked for celebrations in different areas.
  •  This festival is celebrated around March each year. 
  • It is linked to the Hindu lunar calendar, hence its date according to the Gregorian calendar varies. 

 Additional Information 

  • There are two variants of the Shigmo festival: Dhakto Shigmo which is a small Shigmo and Vhadlo Shigmo which is a big Shigmo.
  • Dhakto Shigmo is generally celebrated by farmers, the labor class, and the rural population
  • While Vhadlo Shigmo is of greater consequence and is celebrated by everyone together.

 Important Points

  • Goa is a state in western India with coastlines stretching along the Arabian Sea. 
  • Its long history as a Portuguese colony prior to 1961 is evident in its preserved 17th-century churches and the area’s tropical spice plantations. 
  • Goa is also known for its beaches, ranging from popular stretches at Baga and Palolem to those in laid-back fishing villages such as Agonda.
